definitions.explanation: To come into possession of something, especially something that required effort or was difficult to find. Often implies that the item was not easily available.

examples.japanese: チケットを{入手|にゅうしゅ}した。
{限定|げんてい}グッズを{入手|にゅうしゅ}するのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's hard to get hold of limited-edition goods.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{犯人|はんにん}に{関|かん}する{新|あら}たな{情報|じょうほう}を{入手|にゅうしゅ}した。
examples.english: The police obtained new information regarding the suspect.

notes:
{入手|にゅうしゅ}する emphasizes the act of successfully acquiring something, often implying effort or difficulty. It is slightly more formal than もらう or {手|て}に{入|い}れる.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {情報|じょうほう}を{入手|にゅうしゅ}する (obtain information)
- チケットを{入手|にゅうしゅ}する (get a ticket)
- {資料|しりょう}を{入手|にゅうしゅ}する (acquire materials/documents)
- {入手|にゅうしゅ}{困難|こんなん} (difficult to obtain)
- {入手|にゅうしゅ}{可能|かのう} (obtainable, available)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手|て}に{入|い}れる: similar meaning but slightly more casual
- もらう: to receive (from someone) — no nuance of effort
- {入手|にゅうしゅ}する: implies active effort to acquire
